extracted.intended_audience: general literate readers interested in travel, art, theatre, and social reform (mid-19th-century cultural observers)
extracted.subtask_description: A literary travelogue / series of letters describing social institutions, theatre, art, music, and daily life in London and Paris, mixing personal anecdote with cultural criticism and reform-minded observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison as a redemption school
rubrics_metrics.description: Prisons should be considered and organized as 'redemption schools' rather than merely places of confinement; Pentonville shows neatness, order, kindness, and good judgment but also an air of bleak forlornness and falls short of what is required of such abodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and discipline should aim at moral and social redemption (not only cleanliness and order). Avoid environments that are bleak and dehumanizing; thoughtful, calm, and leisurely reform-minded planning is needed rather than hasty technical fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-cost bathing and washing establishments for the poor
rubrics_metrics.description: Bathing and washing institutions should be made available at very low rates to enable the poor to avoid the miseries of inadequate washing and bathing; the London model provided tubs, heated water, rinsing/drying/ironing apparatus and allowed a poor woman to do in three hours what might otherwise occupy days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities should be efficient (heated water, good tubs, drying closets, apparatus for rinsing/ironing), affordable, and ideally financially sustainable ('promises to pay'). Drying closets reduce exposure and disease risk; such establishments are preliminary and desirable steps toward broader social improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crèches (day nurseries) for working poor women
rubrics_metrics.description: Crèches are houses where poor women leave their children to be nursed during the day while they are at work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Day nurseries enable women's labor and protect children; they are socially beneficial not only in times of acute poverty but remain useful as long as wage disparities exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good acting: naturalism and avoidance of bombast
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatre should be 'living'—acting without stage strut or vulgar bombast; movement rapid, clear, and free; dialogue natural, dignified, and flowing; characters marked with few but distinct strokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exaggerated, bombastic delivery and artificial stage mannerisms. Consistent, uniformly good representation (no lapses into caricature) will be preferred by audiences when given the choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic acting: concentrated expression and sustained purity (Mademoiselle Rachel)
rubrics_metrics.description: A great tragic actor concentrates expression (power in a fixed look or a single word), shows grandeur, truth, and depth, and represents characters with sustained purity of conception; excels in darker passions and desolate grief while may lack softer pathos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not violate the inner harmony of a character to produce momentary effect; sustained, austere conception and truthfulness of expression are central. Range limitations are permissible if the artist achieves depth and purity in their strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting balance: ensure supporting actors match principal talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when one performer is of genius, weak supporting actors (e.g., male actors beside a great female tragic actor) produce an unfortunate on-stage contrast that distracts and creates an additional 'tragedy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting and ensemble quality must be balanced: principal genius should not be undermined by mediocre co-actors; the whole cast should sustain the level required by the play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentimental/dramatic acting: purity, tenderness, and believable grief
rubrics_metrics.description: In sentimental drama, the effective actress embodies purity, lovely tenderness, a mixture of naïveté and piquancy; however, some performers fail to render grief convincingly (they cannot weep or bear the light of day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers in sentimental roles should convey natural tenderness and make grief believable; avoid performers whose mannerisms render sorrow unconvincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical small pieces: topical wit and constant drolleries
rubrics_metrics.description: Small theatre pieces that review leading topics of the day should be full of drolleries that make audiences laugh at each instant (topical satire works well in little theatres).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topicality, lightness, and frequent comic beats are virtues in short satirical pieces; effective lampooning of contemporary figures/events is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to contemporary events requires local promptness and networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Galleries and museums are liberally open to strangers, but contemporary events (lectures, trials, theatrical premieres) are often monopolized by locals who get in early or employ networks to secure admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stranger must plan ahead, secure billets/tickets, and rely on local knowledge or promptness to attend live events; expect competition for popular occasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of a good public lecture
rubrics_metrics.description: A model lecture (exemplified by Arago) is clear, rapid, full, and equal in delivery; such qualities justify the time and effort spent by audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lecturers should aim for clarity, a brisk pace, comprehensive content, and balanced delivery; popularity may require early arrival from listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oratory should draw inferences and give context
rubrics_metrics.description: An orator may be brilliant in detail, but neglecting to draw obvious inferences can weaken the perspective provided to the audience (as in Rémusat's discourse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good speeches should not only present facts and discriminating detail but also synthesize and state the implications and inferences that give the subject its proper point of view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debate and rhetoric: rhetorical polish versus earnest simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetorical readiness, adroitness, and polish can win applause, but a simple, earnest speaker who speaks few unadorned words can create a stronger sense of presence and truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both rhetorical skill and sincerity have value; speakers should beware of substituting ornament for substance, and value plain, heartfelt expression when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should present an adequate outward symbol of interior life
rubrics_metrics.description: True art presents an adequate outward symbol of some fact in the interior life; modern French school tends toward melodrama and exaggeration that lack the 'mystery' and depth of genuine art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists should study Nature’s method, aim to evoke depth and mystery through well-chosen symbols rather than resorting to crude exaggeration (avoid streams of blood for suffering or ghastly contortions for wickedness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Great art requires great thought adequately expressed
rubrics_metrics.description: A great work of art demands a great thought or a thought of beauty adequately expressed; ordinary thought cannot be made profoundly interesting merely by elegant dressing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works on the depth of their underlying thought and how well it is masterfully expressed; be cautious about praising novelty or manner without substantive intellectual content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation of experimental/mystical art (Turner example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Late Turner’s works aim at primitive and elemental forms and effects (light, shadow, contours), which mystify some viewers while eliciting transcendent admiration in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such works may require patient, devout looking to discern intended effects; recognize that transitionary or experimental art can be of value even if controversial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and museum models should be accurate and instructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Botanical wax models with microscopic dissections reveal the 'beautiful secrets' of species and have educational value for museums and universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Museums and educational institutions should acquire and display accurate, detailed scientific models to advance learning; such models should faithfully represent microscopic structure and species variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opera performance: singers must match musical and dramatic demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Orchestral and scenic magnificence are not enough; singers must fill parts with natural beauty, proper intonation and taste—avoid forced, coarse, showy vocalization or meretricious/mechanical expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting should prioritize vocal taste, natural force, poetic dignity, and expressive range appropriate to roles; avoid elevating loudness or mere vocal display above artistic harmony and characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic hygiene: prefer professional laundering and avoid indoor drying
rubrics_metrics.description: Washing done professionally and drying outdoors (or in good drying closets) reduces exposure, mitigates health risks, and is more efficient than household washing days; poor families often cannot afford such services and suffer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote public/private laundries and drying facilities to improve public health and domestic wellbeing; social reform should aim to make such services affordable and widespread.
